content.thinking:
I'm figuring out the loft section orientation for the tube — width along the binormal axis, height along normal — and considering using a box-shaped cross-section to get a blocky, skull-like snout shape.

I'll use a hex-ngon section instead for a dragonish prism look on the snout, with vertices aligned vertex-to-vertex along the ry axis. Setting up a skull-space coordinate function to scale and offset points, then starting the actual implementation with imports for the builder, outline, frame, path, and paint utilities.

Writing imports and helper setup...

For the rune textures, I'm sketching out a glyph set as SVG path strokes within a unit box, designing seven distinct rune shapes using simple line and diamond patterns.

Designing rune glyph paths...

Mapping meters to pixels with a 1000x scale, I'm placing 12 runes along the inner curve edge spaced across the x-range, and working out their rotation angle from the curve's slope while accounting for the y-axis flip between math and screen coordinates.

I'm also planning faint guide polylines along the rune band and some sweeping ember-line accents near the tip, and now moving on to defining the blade's top curve control points first before anything else depends on them.

Writing curve points...

Combining topS and reversed innS to form the outline, marking the tip as sharp, and double-checking the two curves don't cross each other near the tip. Now I'm starting to define the blade paint function for shading.

Still defining feather barb geometry...

Maybe darker bone paint for the barb. Now placing teal flame cards along the spine between barbs at evenly spaced x positions, facing upward with width running along x so they read correctly from the side, sized to roughly match the barb height.

I'll give the flame cards cross:true so two perpendicular tris make the fire read from any angle, since glow() just takes the mesh array from cards. Skipping skull-top flame but adding mouth soul flames positioned at the jaw after posing, with chain and lantern staying as is.

For the eye texture I'm designing an almond-shaped SVG path with a gradient-filled iris, a slit pupil, and a dark rim stroke, aiming for a teal-cyan-white glow against the dark socket.

Now I'm working out how to decal the eye onto the socket sphere, computing the surface point from the socket center plus an outward direction, then slanting the almond shape angrily inward-down using a roll rotation — positive roll for the eye on the +x side so its outer corner lifts upward, mirrored for the other side.

Setting up skull part definitions...

With a hexagonal section I'm getting flat side faces and a bottom vertex, which actually works fine for teeth placement. I'm also weighing a "box" section instead, since that blockier puppet-like shape with a flat bottom might suit the aesthetic better.

Working out the hexagon vertex geometry for the snout, placing teeth at the lower corners so their base aligns with the slanted edge down to the bottom vertex tip.

I'm sketching helper functions for the tooth rows, lower jaw loft, and station interpolation, then planning to write the full build code inline, including the vertebra spline setup.

Keeping the vertebra shaft straight along the y-axis for simplicity, and laying out the vertebra positions in segments—lower, grip, and upper—with slight radius scaling as y increases.

Writing lathe geometry code...

Adding gold bands and collar rings...

Adjusting vertebra positions so they meet the collar, then working out the talon geometry—placing three claw-like forms at 120-degree intervals around the base using bezier curves, with tapered end caps to give each talon a pointed tip.

Adding a center spike that doesn't touch the floor, then setting up a gold collar and torus ring around the shaft with ribbons hanging from beneath it.

Still placing ribbon frames...

I'm sizing two sets of ribbons -- longer front/back ones and shorter side ones -- and sketching the SVG texture for the ribbon cloth: an indigo gradient background, gold border, and a swallowtail notch cut into the top edge where it attaches.

Adding dragon emblem markup...

I'm checking whether the emblem position at the plate center clashes with the cranium's geometry, computing the skull sphere's surface depth and vertical extent to confirm the emblem sits clear of the cranium at that x,y location.

Looking closer, the collar geometry pokes into the plate's front face at that position, so I'll shift the plate back to x=0.13 and adjust its z-depth to -0.13 to clear the collar entirely.

Checking the horn and counter-horn positions against the blade and plate planes, both sitting at z=-0.13, and confirming the left counter-horn stays clear of the skull horns since their x and y ranges don't overlap.

Now I'm working out the lantern placement hanging below the counter-horn tip near x=-0.55, and establishing the blade's origin and local coordinate frame so I can position rune planes, bevel thickness, and edge glow consistently around it.

I'm checking z-fighting risks between rune planes, blade faces, and glow bands—adjusting thicknesses and offsets (blade ±0.015, runes ±0.0185, glow ±0.018) to keep surfaces from overlapping, then sizing the rib rods' radius so they protrude slightly without clipping into the blade.

Since the rune plane is a transparent rectangle covering the whole blade region, any overlap with ribs just gets alpha-cut away, so that's fine. I'm now placing eight tapered ribs per face along the blade (16 total), running diagonally from top to inner edge, and figuring out what bone-colored material to use for them.

I'm also planning a small bone talon curving down from the root plate, built from a tapered bezier sweep like a claw shape in the same flat plane as the blade.

I need to check the ribbon placement doesn't collide with that claw, then position the glowing soul orbs and ghost card elements beneath the inner edge of the blade, roughly between x 0.6-1.1.

For the ghosts, I'm working out whether they should trail toward the blade like they're being pulled in, with tails flowing upward toward the edge rather than hanging below like typical ghosts.

Writing lantern texture SVG...

Now I'm ready to write the actual build function, checking part options like scale, rotation, and decal types before committing to the full code structure, then defining the palette, textures, joints, and parts in sequence.

Defining ivory and stain colors for the bone material...

Still writing the boneColor shading function...

Setting up material definitions for gold, leather, and dark tones, then placing eye socket geometry with decal mapping for the glow effect.

Now I'm working out tooth color and positioning logic, defining an interpolation function to place teeth along the jaw with varying sizes, including larger canines at specific z-coordinates for each side of the jaw.

Still placing teeth...

For the forehead gem, I'm trying to find a surface point on the cranium using a projection helper, but need to guard against a null hit if the ray doesn't intersect.

Then I'm positioning crest spikes along the back of the head at specific azimuth and elevation angles, adding a neck connector rod between the head and body, and planning the jaw-area flame effects based on the mouth gap geometry.

I'm placing three flame cards at different z-depths along the jaw, checking that each gap between jaw top and snout bottom is large enough for the flame heights I want, and sizing each flame root accordingly so they fit within the mouth opening without clipping. I also want to consider whether a card should face sideways so the flame reads correctly from both front and side views.

Now I'm writing a helper for ring/torus pieces that takes a bone, position, direction, radius, and color, then using it to build a chain of alternating torus links climbing up with slight scale and rotation offsets to suggest twisted links.

Next I'm working out the lantern geometry below the chain — placing the final cap, finial ring, and glass cylinder positions by stacking y-offsets so the lantern hangs cleanly beneath the last chain link.

The torus uses its default axis orientation since it's already lying flat in the vertical plane, matching the chain link position near the ring center. Now I'm setting up the lantern and chain bone hierarchy, with the lantern joint parented to the snath pointing downward.

Writing SVG flame texture...

Now I'm shaping the ghost's wavy-tailed body with gradient fill, dark eye and mouth ellipses, and a deep teal outline, then moving on to design an eye icon in a wide viewBox...

Writing eye SVG shape...

Checking the b.stick signature, then working out the ringed spikes arrangement around the blade—since the frame has no bone assignment, I need to figure out which joint the geometry should attach to, likely the nearest one to the snath/head area.

I'll place the head joint near the top and the snath root lower, letting the bone assignment default to whichever is closest for parts without an explicit bone. The plan feels settled now, so I'm moving to write the full file before running a typecheck and preview.
